retry_attribution.conclusion: Repeated500 setup calls are attributable to the native harness SDK retry path, not new run_episodes/episode attempts. Native runner retry0 does not bound received provider HTTP arrivals to one per episode.

deterministic_fixture_identity_defect.fact: Frozen fixture uses the global received-arrival index to choose dev-good only when index==2; otherwise fixture-good selects final-once. Failed arrivals still consume that index.
deterministic_fixture_identity_defect.source_derived_mechanism: After dev-bad consumes arrivals1 and2, the next native dev-good call is arrival3. Its normal fixture-good request would select final-once, for which phase2 has no reservation; the exact-row assertion therefore returns500. Arrivals4and5 fail the existing index<=3 cap.

No raw request or stack location was retained for those three failures because recording follows the assertions, so identification of arrival3 specifically with that SQL assertion is a source-derived diagnosis, rather than a directly logged assertion line.

earliest_delay_hypothesis.proposal: The controller performs its first heavy ChatDialect/Verifiers import inside FixtureHandler.answer before sending any response. Cold import on the first provider request can explain crossing the3s read timeout; the retry reaches already imported code and succeeds.
earliest_delay_hypothesis.support: Exact frozen source places the import in the firstPOST path, the first call times out around3.025s, the first late write breaks, and the same request/body succeeds afterward.
earliest_delay_hypothesis.unverified: No import-duration/profile, original received monotonic, response-prepared timestamp or original timeout traceback was retained. The handler overwrites arrival monotonic when preparing a response. General scheduling/resource/transport delay remains an alternative; causal cold-import attribution is not established.
